# Truck Box

> Truck Box is the DAT One broker emailer built for truck dispatchers, carriers, and owner-operators. It speeds up the DAT One load board (one.dat.com) across dry van, flatbed, and reefer loads, adding one-click broker emails, Google Maps routes, a deadhead-adjusted rate-per-mile, a miles filter, and keyboard navigation. Works in Google Chrome and Opera, with secure Google sign-in.

## What it does

- One-click broker email: a custom template auto-fills from the load's data on DAT and sends from your own Gmail. No copy-paste, no second tab. It only sends email you choose to send and never reads your inbox.
- Google Maps in one click: open the load's route as three stops — your truck location, the pickup, and the destination.
- RPM with deadhead: a true rate-per-mile that includes the empty miles to pickup, plus total miles including deadhead, so you see the real economics of a load.
- Miles filter: hide loads shorter than the distance you set.
- Keyboard navigation: move through the board and act without the mouse.
- Broker / factoring credit check: vet who is posting before you call (coming soon).

## Who it is for

- Truck dispatchers, carriers, and owner-operators sourcing freight on DAT One.
- Works across equipment types: dry van, flatbed, and reefer loads.

## Compatibility

- Browsers: Google Chrome and Opera (Chromium-based browsers).
- Sign-in: secure Google sign-in.
- Privacy: sends email only; never reads your inbox.

## Pricing

- 7-day free trial, no credit card required.

## FAQ

- What does Truck Box do? It adds one-click broker emailing, route maps, deadhead-adjusted RPM, a miles filter, and keyboard navigation to the DAT One load board so dispatchers book loads faster.
- Who is it for? Truck dispatchers, carriers, and owner-operators on DAT One.
- What load types does it support? Any DAT One load, including dry van, flatbed, and reefer.
- Which browsers are supported? Google Chrome and Opera.
- How much does it cost? It starts with a 7-day free trial, no credit card required.
- Does it read my email? No. It only sends emails you explicitly choose to send from your own Gmail.
